source_correspondence: The earlier displayed coefficient-gradient estimate omitted the time derivative. It is now explicitly included in LP3, the physical homogeneous formula LP4 and the energy estimate LP24.

The fixed smooth nonnegative coefficient is extended in all time and phase variables. FP0:S1 gives the full time-space gradient bound; scalar Fefferman–Phong is then applied in the transverse variables at each fixed time. The time derivative is a coefficient symbol, not a time derivative of the input.

Taylor bounds give alpha_t of size delta and each transverse derivative of order k of size delta to the power 1-k. The same cutoff product, finite Weyl remainders and width-before-frequency choice therefore control the time term with exactly the claimed square-root-frequency gain.

The example alpha=t squared plus x squared checks the full gradient, localized time term and its operator product correction. Six new exact identities bring the total to 43. No new exercise or supplement is counted.

The time term supplies the missing coefficient for commutators against weights depending on the frequency dual to time. The general propagation theorem is still pending; no such theorem is asserted by this correction.
Reduced-leaf propagation proves the superharmonic and conic conclusions. One-dimensional descent and semidefinite propagation retain the full real-order and clock hypotheses.

The geometric width is chosen before its frequency threshold. Every use of a width-dependent symbol seminorm is followed by a frequency choice at that fixed width; no uniform threshold over all shrinking neighborhoods is asserted.

The exact constant metric has Planck parameter lambda. Earlier complete finite products, quantization conversion and scalar constant-metric Fefferman–Phong proofs provide all remainders. The scaled scalar lower bound is order lambda squared.

The fixed nonnegative coefficient is extended before localization. Its full gradient form has a lambda-squared error independent of the shrinking cutoff. A separate positivity argument gives the limiting operator norm from the symbol maximum.

Second-order vanishing of the nonnegative coefficient, first-order vanishing of the real factor and every cutoff derivative give the exact delta-squared, delta and unit commutator sizes, including near the time endpoints.

The sandwich operators are positive or self-adjoint as required, bounded at each frequency and norm-continuous in time. Both nested commutators are expanded as symbols before their operator norms are estimated.

The Nirenberg–Treves product is O(delta). Both Hilbert estimates apply with the exact D_t sign. The complete left-quantized product error is O(delta), so the original operator has both the solution and retained positive-energy bounds.

The two energy products have identical principal symbols and vanishing first corrections. Every second correction has four derivatives against an initial delta-to-the-fourth factor. All complete form errors are uniformly bounded after choosing the frequency threshold.

Multiplication by the extra cutoff gives exactly power four in the differentiated coefficient symbols. The first product and left/Weyl corrections are uniformly bounded. The physical base and frequency derivatives carry their distinct powers and give the square-root-frequency gain.

The variable-power forward implication retains every logarithmic derivative and a finite microlocal partition with strict local Sobolev margins. Compact distributions have an explicit finite negative Sobolev order.

The converse constructs a finite complex-weight inverse with a strict margin. Its recursively cancelled coefficients, support, logarithmic bounds, weighted tails and quantitative remainder on H-minus-M are explicit.

The uniform shell bound is integrated as an actual L2-valued integral. The resulting symbol is homogeneous at high frequency and positive on the chosen ray. An exact earlier elliptic parametrix recovers the regularity index without asserting endpoint membership.
The corrected reader has 314 parsed formulae, 36 numbered displays and fifteen inspected captures. The original reproducible scale figure and its exact coordinate review remain valid.

component_scope: Two scales enter propagation through a degenerate characteristic interval. The geometric width makes the commutators small. The frequency parameter then makes the quantization errors small at that fixed width. We prove the full localized estimates with this order of choices, and characterize the microlocal Sobolev index by variable powers on frequency shells.
